# Ting 0.6.1
## Changes
- **An Accessibility window instead of an error.** When a micro-app needs Accessibility (the selected text, the front window, `keys`, `paste` or `output.to: [app]`) and Ting does not have it, Ting opens a window with the steps: **Open Accessibility Settings** opens System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility, and the Ting icon in the window can be dragged straight into its list of apps. The window stays above System Settings and closes by itself once access is on; then start the micro-app again. A result that could not be pasted stays on the clipboard. Ting no longer shows the prompt of macOS for it. - **Accessibility in Settings.** Settings › Advanced shows whether Ting has Accessibility; **Allow…** opens the same window. - **Readable buttons in the light theme.** Prominent buttons, such as **Continue** in the welcome window, use a lighter amber, so their text stands out.
## Upgrade and install
Requires **macOS 14 or later**. The universal ZIP supports **Apple Silicon and Intel**.
To upgrade an installed copy, choose **Check for Updates…** in the menu-bar menu. Your settings, leader, bindings, micro-apps and permissions are kept.
For a new or manual installation, download `Ting-0.6.1-universal.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/bobuk-io/ting/releases/latest) and unzip it. Quit any running copy of Ting, move `Ting.app` to `/Applications` (replace the old copy for a manual upgrade), and open it. Ting lives in the menu bar and has no Dock icon. On first launch, choose a leader key; there is no default leader.
The official release is signed with Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and includes a stapled notarization ticket. Verify the archive with `SHA256SUMS.txt` if desired. Ting asks for Automation and Accessibility only when a micro-app needs them (see the [0.6.0 release notes](v0.6.0.md#permissions)) and never for Input Monitoring.
